decision: started from merged main at d0c1b39
why: measure release work against the verified analyzer, not the feature branch
result: baseline fixed

decision: kept the package at the repository root
why: this is one CLI and library package; a monorepo would add paths and release coordination without removing complexity
result: root package retained

decision: defined release readiness as clean install, checks, audit, packed CLI proof, repository policy files, and a reproducible publish path
why: each condition can be checked from a clean clone without trusting this run's summary
result: predicate set

decision: added a package verification skill backed by a real tarball consumer
why: package-source tests can miss files, exports, lifecycle behavior, and version drift at the published boundary
result: pack, install, CLI scan/compare/rules, library import, and no-edit proof passed

decision: kept the verification controller in one repository script
why: the CLI is short-lived and the release predicate needs one deterministic command, not a controller framework
result: verification surface kept small

decision: prepared @ocarinalabs/effect-doctor 0.1.0 for public npm publication
why: 0.0.0 and private true made publication impossible; the scoped name is available and 0.1.0 communicates an initial supported release
result: public dry run passed with no manifest repair warning

decision: derived the runtime doctor version from package.json
why: a second literal drifted under ordinary version bumps and could mislabel CLI output and reports
result: package and runtime versions agree at 0.1.0

decision: stopped emitting source and declaration maps
why: the package omitted src, so the maps pointed to files users could not inspect; dropping broken artifacts reduced the archive without widening the package surface
result: archive reduced to 100 files and 456327 unpacked bytes

decision: validated provider spans against snapshotted source and filtered diagnostics by detected Effect version
why: provider output was schema-shaped but could still produce empty evidence, invalid public positions, or v4-only findings in v3 files
evidence: 74 tests; bun run check; bun run audit
result: out-of-bounds and zero-based diagnostics fail closed; unsupported-version Oxlint diagnostics abstain

decision: split provider normalization into boundary, policy, and construction helpers
why: the first fail-closed implementation crossed Fallow cognitive-complexity thresholds
result: zero complexity and duplication findings above threshold

decision: made exported report schemas enforce scanner invariants
why: consumers could previously decode a successful report with no engines, incomplete coverage, or a false summary
result: exact complete provider receipts, matching inventories and versions, accurate summaries, and coherent comparison counts are required

decision: made wrapped generator detection return the unwrapped function node
why: the previous type guard claimed a transparent wrapper was the generator, so range identity silently missed the throw
result: wrapped generator throw is reported

decision: scoped unsafe Chunk wrap ordering to one execution boundary
why: lexical order across a deferred nested function is not runtime order and produced a false positive
result: deferred wrap abstains while four straight-line mutations remain reported

decision: exported the typed failure cases from the package root
why: scanProject exposes DoctorFailure in its Effect error channel, so consumers need names they can import without a forbidden internal path
result: fresh consumer imported all three runtime error classes from the package name

decision: bounded each analyzer output stream at 16 MiB and replaced inherited environment with a platform allowlist
why: unbounded buffering allowed memory exhaustion and full environment inheritance exposed unrelated credentials to analyzer children
result: over-limit output fails closed and a parent sentinel secret is absent in the child

decision: rewrote the landing path around requirements, one successful scan, CLI exits, comparison, and the public API
why: the previous README began with internal policy and left installation, root tsconfig, Node floor, and error JSON implicit
evidence: README.md; markdown link check; clean fixture CLI output
result: install-first reader path is self-contained

decision: added contribution, conduct, support, security, changelog, issue, pull-request, and release contracts
why: public package users and contributors need explicit ownership and private-reporting paths before publication
evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md; SECURITY.md; SUPPORT.md; CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md; CHANGELOG.md; .github templates
result: community and disclosure surface defined without inventing a contact address

decision: kept repository visibility and npm provenance as an explicit release gate
why: changing a private repository to public is a separate authorization decision; private source can use OIDC but cannot generate npm provenance
result: no visibility or publication side effect performed

decision: removed one narrative configuration comment and kept the proven TaggedError compatibility note
why: Comment Sicko found one redundant narration and no MUST KILL comments
result: one comment deleted, no suppressions or protocol fixtures removed

decision: packed only current user documentation and removed broken research links
why: the prior installed README referenced files absent from the tarball
result: 109 files, 76626 compressed bytes, 485199 unpacked bytes; required docs present and no source maps

decision: made CI exercise the release predicate on Linux, macOS, and Windows with pinned actions and read-only permissions
why: package consumers span all three operating systems and movable action tags widen the supply-chain boundary
result: 84 tests, dependency audit, Fallow, self-scan, installed tarball consumer, and dry-run pack passed locally

decision: added an exact-tag OIDC publishing workflow without publishing
why: a release must match package.json and should not store a long-lived npm token; repository visibility and first publication remain explicit gates
result: matching v0.1.0 succeeds, mismatched tags fail, workflow YAML parses

decision: added weekly Bun and GitHub Actions updates plus a high-severity dependency audit
why: Fallow audits source structure rather than registry advisories, so both checks are required
result: no vulnerabilities across 256 packages

decision: made installed CLI verification portable across npm shims
why: Windows cmd shims cannot be launched reliably through the same direct process call used on Unix
result: all platforms require a generated shim; Windows drives the installed entrypoint with Node while Unix drives the shim

decision: set repository workflow defaults to read-only, disabled workflow pull-request approvals, and required immutable action SHAs
why: least privilege should be enforced by GitHub as well as declared inside workflow files
result: default read, approvals false, SHA pinning required

decision: enabled Dependabot vulnerability alerts
why: weekly update pull requests do not cover newly disclosed vulnerabilities between runs
result: endpoint now returns 204 enabled

decision: ran the pstack Interrogate gate with four independent model configurations
why: one reviewer can miss a release-path or runtime-contract failure; identical intent and rubric make disagreements inspectable
evidence: gpt-5.6-sol max; gpt-5.6-terra ultra; gpt-5.6-luna max; gpt-5.5 xhigh
result: all P1 and reproducible P2 findings acted on; recursive reviewer fan-out was interrupted

decision: split release verification from environment-gated OIDC publishing and transferred one hashed tarball
why: the prior job approved before verification, ran tag code with OIDC, and repacked after testing
result: stable main-ancestor tags produce an artifact without OIDC; the gated no-checkout job hash-checks and publishes exact bytes

decision: left automated npm publishing disabled behind NPM_TRUSTED_PUBLISHING_ENABLED
why: the private repository currently has no protected npm environment and the first npm package version does not exist
result: bootstrap remains manual from the verified artifact; no environment auto-created and no package published

decision: made exported report schemas enforce paths, inventories, fingerprints, ordering, and the exact comparison delta
why: plausible counts previously allowed fabricated reports that hid introduced or resolved findings
result: absolute, traversal, Windows-style, out-of-inventory, forged-fingerprint, unsorted, and false-delta reports fail decoding

decision: validated Oxlint UTF-8 byte columns and configured pass, activation, and severity policy
why: valid Unicode diagnostics failed while disabled or wrong-severity diagnostics could be accepted
result: Unicode evidence normalizes and provider drift fails closed

decision: made package tests and npm invocation portable across Windows paths and command shims
why: cross-platform CI would fail on literal POSIX test roots, slash guards, and direct npm cmd execution
result: platform path primitives and Node-driven npm CLI are used on Windows

decision: added installed-consumer declaration typechecking and explicit comparison API typing
why: inferred declarations emitted a source-only errors.ts reference at the public boundary
result: public declarations use errors.js and the fresh consumer typecheck passes

decision: expanded package verification to failure envelopes, unknown rules, and archive-only dependency installation
why: documented failure paths were not driven and an explicitly installed Effect dependency could mask manifest drift
result: installed package alone supplies its runtime graph and both exit-2 contracts pass

decision: added a stable AnalyzerFailure reason channel
why: timeout and output-limit failures were mislabeled as startup failures
result: process, timeout, output-limit, exit, and toolchain causes remain distinguishable

decision: reran Ultracite, TypeScript, Vitest, Fallow, self-analysis, and retained-artifact verification
why: the fixes crossed runtime, schema, packaging, and workflow boundaries and required one shared predicate
evidence: bun run check; bun run audit; bun run doctor:self; .verification/effect-doctor/2026-08-30T09-48-13-555Z-65863
result: 96 tests, zero lint issues, zero Fallow issues, clean three-provider scan, 111-file tarball, and matching SHA-256 passed

decision: updated the model-test count from 12 to 13
why: the audit is append-only and the canonical inventory-order regression was added after the preceding evidence row
result: 13 model tests pass

decision: superseded the 96-test intermediate result with the final 97-test release predicate
why: the canonical inventory-order regression increased the suite after the earlier evidence row
result: 97 tests, zero dependency vulnerabilities, zero lint or Fallow issues, clean self-scan, installed package proof, and 111-file dry-run pack passed

decision: moved three deliberate red-phase verification runs to Trash
why: only successful evidence should remain in the repository-local ignored evidence tree
result: failed proofs remain recoverable in Trash; no failure.json remains under .verification

decision: narrowed the machine-readable verification claim to the installed-package proof
why: verification.json records package, rule, scan, comparison, export, and status data but does not encode every preceding release command
result: aggregate command results and machine-readable package evidence are now distinguished

decision: replaced the earlier scoped-name availability claim with a registry-absence claim
why: npm E404 proves that the public package was absent at capture time, not that the scope is owned or publication is authorized
result: ownership and first-publication authority remain explicit release gates

decision: retained the Interrogate findings and dispositions in the repository
why: the earlier audit named reviewer configurations without preserving an inspectable consolidated report
result: all reproducible P1 and P2 findings map to fixes or verification assertions; none were dismissed

decision: captured external GitHub and npm state relevant to release gating
why: repository settings, environments, alerts, and package absence are external mutable facts and should not be inferred from workflow source
result: private visibility, read-only workflow defaults, SHA pinning, enabled alerts, zero environments, and npm E404 recorded as a point-in-time snapshot

decision: reran the independent release-audit reviewer after correcting the evidence trail
why: the same different-model reviewer should confirm its findings were resolved rather than trusting the implementation pass
result: prior flags resolved; no remaining actionable P1-P3 audit-evidence defect
